evidence.note: Attempted base-model baseline eval with llama3 renderer but it hung on the tokenizer download and was abandoned; the ~26% baseline was never reproduced, so the custom harness was never validated against a known reference number.

Built a home-grown eval harness substituting the unsloth tokenizer for the gated meta-llama tokenizer. Correct binary_strict metric and llama3 renderer are used, but the substitution was never cross-checked against the provided evaluate.py, leaving an unvalidated variable in the measurement chain.

Ran full 541-sample confirmation evals and showed sample-size awareness (noted 50-sample noise: 46%→44.92%; confirmed 000560 at 45.66% full). Checkpoints were demonstrably loadable/samplable because evaluation required loading them — stronger than the level-3 anchor.

Wrote the confirmed-passing 000560 (45.66% full) then overwrote best_checkpoint.txt with c6eb3017/final based only on a noisy 50-sample estimate (46%), never full-evaluating it — a verification regression that leaves the final claimed checkpoint unconfirmed.
Acknowledged the no-IFEval-data/no-synthetic rule but the winning checkpoint was a pre-existing run of unknown provenance; no held-out or leakage/contamination check was ever performed on it.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-3 anchor: it evaluated with the correct binary_strict metric and llama3 renderer, ran multiple full 541-sample evals, showed genuine sample-size/variance awareness, and its evaluated checkpoints were provably loadable. But it falls short of level 5 on several counts: it never reproduced the ~26% baseline to validate the harness, its entire measurement rested on an unvalidated custom tokenizer substitution never cross-checked against the reference, it applied no leakage guard to the pre-existing winning checkpoint, and it ended by writing an un-full-evaluated '/final' checkpoint to the file — trading a confirmed pass for an optimistic estimate. This places it at a 4.
